abstract.p: This paper presents an in-depth study on multimodal hate speech detection in Dravidian languages-Tamil, Telugu, and Malayalam-by leveraging both audio and text modalities. Detecting hate speech in these languages is particularly challenging due to factors such as code-mixing, limited linguistic resources, and diverse cultural contexts. Our approach integrates advanced techniques for audio feature extraction and XLM-Roberta for text representation, with feature alignment and fusion to develop a robust multimodal framework. The dataset is carefully categorized into labeled classes: gender-based, political, religious, and personal defamation hate speech, along with a non-hate category. Experimental results indicate that our model achieves a macro F1-score of 0.76 and an accuracy of approximately 85
